raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`baidu/Unlimited-OCR` crashes at startup with a bare `AssertionError` on any
backend that needs a paged KV cache. Every layer of the model uses sliding-window
attention, so SGLang picks `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator`. That allocator only
supported `page_size == 1`: it asserted it in `__init__`, and `alloc_extend` /
`alloc_decode` raised `NotImplementedError`.

## Modifications

- add `page_size=1` as supported page_size for XPU backend.

Prefer aligning XPU with CUDA over an XPU-only allocator path.

The all-SWA crash comes from `_intel_xpu_page_constraint` rewriting page_size to 128, which then hits `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` assert `page_size == 1`. CUDA's default MHA path (fa3 / flashinfer / triton) stays at `page_size == 1` and already serves this allocator. XPU should do the same: leave an unset page size at 1, and do not snap it to 64/128.

NOTICE that `page_size == 1` is already a real kernel path, not a missing feature. `XPUAttentionBackend._forward_attn_flat_page_table` reshapes the KV cache to (tokens, 1, heads, dim) and calls flash_attn_with_kvcache; the main path only strides and divides the page table when page_size > 1. If some kernel still rejects 1, fix the kernel. Do not teach the shared allocator a paged pure-SWA path just to absorb this rewrite.

I'd go with mingfeima and Valentine233's suggestion of running this model at page_size 1 on XPU instead. As written this isn't XPU-gated, so it turns on pure-SWA with page_size > 1 for every backend, and the tests are mostly mocks. If you keep this approach, the PD-decode crash below needs a fix first.

With page_size > 1 this is now reachable. On PD decode, `_uses_swa_tail_prealloc()` (disaggregation/decode.py:466) returns true for this allocator, so the first transferred request hits this via decode.py:2314 and raises (reproduced at page_size=128). Could you exclude pure-SWA there so decode falls back to `alloc_extend`, or keep rejecting page_size > 1 for PD decode?

Follow-up Intel review of 62829a6c837e: keeping pure-SWA on page size 1 is the right direction, but please address the MLA and graph compatibility boundaries below and add coverage for the motivating pure-SWA path.

I checked the pinned sglang-kernel-xpu 0.4.0 wheel: MHA page size 1 is implemented through KV gathers plus non-paged varlen attention, including a device scalar read; MLA has a separate kernel contract. Eight isolated checks of the exact configuration function passed, but no local XPU inference was run.

The XPU and Xeon jobs executed and passed on this head. Required CUDA coverage is still NOT VERIFIED: the B300 root failure reports CUDA devices busy/unavailable, and several downstream H100/B200/GB300 jobs stopped at the health-check fail-fast gate. This is an infrastructure/coverage blocker, not evidence of a PR-caused CUDA regression; please rerun after runner recovery so the required tests actually execute. Unspecified XPU page size still resolves to 128; this change does not globally switch the default to 1.

**[blocking]** Adding `1` here also permits MLA page size 1, because the MLA branch extends this same list. MLA uses `flash_mla_decode`, whose pinned 0.4.0 kernel explicitly accepts only 16/32/64/128; it does not use the MHA page-size-1 workaround. Please separate the MHA/MLA allowlists and add a regression test ensuring MLA page size 1 is rejected or normalized to a supported size.

+def _dense_page_url() -> str:
+    """A letter-size page large enough to take the tiling path, with one
+    numbered line per row so the transcription is long and checkable."""
+    w, h = 1700, 2200
+    img = Image.new("RGB", (w, h), "white")
+    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)
+    size = h // (NUM_LINES + 8)
+    font = _font(size)
+    draw.text((w // 20, size), "REPORT 0001", fill="black", font=font)
+    for i in range(NUM_LINES):

+            fill="black",
+            font=font,
+        )
+    buffer = io.BytesIO()
+    img.save(buffer, format="PNG")

+
+    @classmethod
+    def setUpClass(cls):
+        cls.model = "baidu/Unlimited-OCR"
+        cls.base_url = DEFAULT_URL_FOR_TEST
+        cls.image_url = _dense_page_url()
+        cls.process = popen_launch_server(

+    def _parse(self, max_tokens: int) -> dict:

+                "messages": [
+                    {
+                        "role": "user",
+                        "content": [
+                            {"type": "text", "text": "document parsing."},
+                            {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": self.image_url}},
+                        ],
+                    }
+                ],
+                "temperature": 0,
+                "max_tokens": max_tokens,
+                "images_config": {"image_mode": "gundam"},
+            },
+            timeout=600,
+        )
+        response.raise_for_status()
+        return response.json()

+    def test_page_size_is_not_rewritten(self):

+    def test_decode_past_sliding_window(self):

+        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as pool:

+        for out in outs:

+            self.assertIn("05. item 4", text)

reviews.body:
Prefer aligning XPU with CUDA over an XPU-only allocator path.

The all-SWA crash comes from `_intel_xpu_page_constraint` rewriting page_size to 128, which then hits `PureSWATokenToKVPoolAllocator` assert `page_size == 1`. CUDA's default MHA path (fa3 / flashinfer / triton) stays at `page_size == 1` and already serves this allocator. XPU should do the same: leave an unset page size at 1, and do not snap it to 64/128.

NOTICE that `page_size == 1` is already a real kernel path, not a missing feature. `XPUAttentionBackend._forward_attn_flat_page_table` reshapes the KV cache to (tokens, 1, heads, dim) and calls flash_attn_with_kvcache; the main path only strides and divides the page table when page_size > 1. If some kernel still rejects 1, fix the kernel. Do not teach the shared allocator a paged pure-SWA path just to absorb this rewrite.

I'd go with mingfeima and Valentine233's suggestion of running this model at page_size 1 on XPU instead. As written this isn't XPU-gated, so it turns on pure-SWA with page_size > 1 for every backend, and the tests are mostly mocks. If you keep this approach, the PD-decode crash below needs a fix first.

Follow-up Intel review of 62829a6c837e: keeping pure-SWA on page size 1 is the right direction, but please address the MLA and graph compatibility boundaries below and add coverage for the motivating pure-SWA path.

I checked the pinned sglang-kernel-xpu 0.4.0 wheel: MHA page size 1 is implemented through KV gathers plus non-paged varlen attention, including a device scalar read; MLA has a separate kernel contract. Eight isolated checks of the exact configuration function passed, but no local XPU inference was run.

The XPU and Xeon jobs executed and passed on this head. Required CUDA coverage is still NOT VERIFIED: the B300 root failure reports CUDA devices busy/unavailable, and several downstream H100/B200/GB300 jobs stopped at the health-check fail-fast gate. This is an infrastructure/coverage blocker, not evidence of a PR-caused CUDA regression; please rerun after runner recovery so the required tests actually execute. Unspecified XPU page size still resolves to 128; this change does not globally switch the default to 1.
